objective: Reduce subsequent human correction work across all Japanese Tç/tç targets, not merely maximize precision on a small selected subset.
reference: Canonical human-reviewed ç typefaces through f484, including Japanese and Portuguese examples; no f485+ label was used for training.
previous_method_problems: Connected-component selection sometimes chose the following u rather than ç.
72-by-48 crops discarded native scan detail before magnification.
The reported 96.8 percent precision covered only 155 of 478 eligible validation cases, with thresholds explored on the same folds. It did not establish high full-coverage accuracy.

method.crop: 144-by-96 scan-derived patches, retaining twice the previous normalized resolution
method.segmentation: Target-position and descender-aware connected-component selection, isotropic resizing with padding
method.features: 48-by-48 glyph image; 4-pixel cells, 8 unsigned gradient orientation bins
method.classifier: StandardScaler followed by balanced LogisticRegression, C=0.01, threshold=0
method.score: Signed decision score, not a calibrated probability

chronological_holdout.test: Every extracted Japanese Tç/tç on f483–f484
chronological_holdout.caveat: These pages had been explored in the earlier experiment; this is a chronological held-out check for the new training run, not a never-seen final benchmark.

page_grouped_validation.coverage: All extracted examples; no confidence-based exclusion
page_grouped_validation.interpretation: Overall accuracy is dominated by easier examples. The relevant recent T section scores 92.4 percent, not 98.2 percent. Rare Italic forms remain difficult.

other_experiments: Corrected segmentation alone, HOG/pixel features, SVM and tree models, wider/tighter crops
An expanded-reference context CNN learned neighboring-language/typeface cues and missed most recent Japanese Italics; rejected
A glyph-only CNN reached approximately the same recent held-out result as HOG, without a compelling gain
Japanese-domain weights 5/20/100 did not solve the rare Italic misses; retained the simpler unweighted HOG recipe
Previously cached styled OCR classified all 503 tested Japanese reference cedillas Roman; not used as a style authority

application.scope: Prepared Japanese Tç/tç targets after f484, found on f485–f542 and f643
application.f485_c1_l001: Italic; model score +6.09, consistent with the user's explicit visual identification
application.preserved: All characters, comments, geometry, non-target typefaces, and pages through f484
application.status: AI-provisional typeface corrections, not human approval
